range.remark: Pss 61-66:12 (national part A of Ps 66); notes on Ps 66:13-20 (part B) begin bottom of pdf 30 -> next batch

entries.note: Leg. the plural נגינות, because elsewhere it is always plural.
The verb עטף in the sense 'to be shrouded in grief, languish' occurs only in Niphal and Hithpael, so here too read the Niphal infinitive.
entries.flag: exact form garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: Gives no intelligible sense — every rock is higher than the one seeking shelter on it; and lead me whither? Pesch. 'Du hast mich erhöht und getröstet', LXX in part likewise (ὕψωσάς με): leg. בצור תרוממני (interchange of י and ת) or מצוררי 'from my foes', and ותנחמני 'and comfort me'.

entries.emendation: a verse is missing, etwa ואני אשיר עזך
entries.note: כי היית cannot speak of an accomplished fact when rescue is only now being implored; it must be an anticipated song, but then a verse announcing the vow to sing must have preceded (cf. vv.6, 9, which speak of a vow made).

ירשת as 'inheritance, possession' is completely unintelligible. Krochmal's emendation ארשת (as Ps 21:3) is inadmissible, being etymologically dark there as well; wohl, as there, leg. משאלת 'the request of those who fear Thy name'.
Vielleicht leg. תוסף (jussive) — the petition to which Ps 21:5 refers (חיים שאל ממך נתתה לו).
מן is inexplicable; leg. כן (interchange of מ and כ, o. S. 199): 'Gnade und Treue werden ihn so bewahren'. The emendation מה' (in Kennicott) does not satisfy.
The suffix on an infinitive with ל is unusual; either leg. לשלם, or בשלמי 'durch meinen Gesang werde ich mein Gelübde täglich leisten'.
The instrument indication after למנצח על is missing, and statt ידותון leg. לידותון (o. S. 87).

Vv.2-3 are decidedly the refrain, like vv.6-7, so both must read exactly alike: in v.2 leg. דומי as v.6, followed by כי ממנו, and תקותי statt ישועתי, which ought not be repeated in the following verse.

entries.emendation: draw רבה to v.4 as a vocative, etwa יְרִיבַי
entries.note: רבה cannot stand at the close of v.3, or it would differ from v.7 — and the word is senseless anyway ('not totter much? but a little?'). Moreover v.4 lacks the subject of the apostrophe עד אנה: draw רבה over and make of it a vocative ('Meine Widersacher, wie lange...').
תרצחו is a strange form, formally and logically unfitting, and lacks the required accusative; easily emended by transposition to תצריחו 'raise a shout of triumph'.
Etymologically inexplicable; it must be synonymous with צרח. Targum תרגשון 'toben', hence תנהמו or the like (the emendations תתהללו, תתקוממו of Hitzig and Hupfeld do not fit).
entries.flag: second proposed alternative garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: כלכם belongs to the following clause; statt גדר leg. the feminine גדרה (Olshausen). But דחויה does not fit — it means only 'push away, thrust out', not 'push over'; leg. רפויה 'gelockert' (interchange of ד and ר, o. S. 135).

Only the psalmist himself can have spoken this verse, so leg. להדיחי (objective suffix on the infinitive, = להדיחני), the י drawn from ירצו; what remains, רצו כזב, is to be pointed רֹצֵי כזב 'those who delight in delusion', i.e. idolatry (o. S. 41) — the opponents want to seduce the singer from God's majesty to idolatry. משאתו: the versions waver between third person and first; the former is more correct, referring to God.
בפיו is surely incorrect; the versions have the plural suffix — leg. בפימו.
עם as bare address is without analogy; leg. עמו, God's people, the Anawim (o. S. 26).
'To go up (or bring up) on the scales'? Unintelligible. The frequent interchange of ע and פ (o. S. 134) leads to a verb meaning 'to weigh' (cf. פלס).
entries.flag: exact form garbled in OCR (לפלות/לפלס?) — verify

entries.note: Statt מהבל wohl leg. הבל: 'sind sie allsammt nur Hauch'.

'One should not trust in oppression and robbery — do the pious first need that admonition?' Parallel Isa 30:12 (ותבטחו בעשק ונלוז), where נלוז is 'the perverse': in both places leg. בעקש statt בעשק, synonymous with נלוז, and the verse is to be divided otherwise than the punctuators give: אל תבטחו בעקש / ובנלוז אל תהבלו — 'Verlasset euch nicht auf den Verkehrten'.
The close is also unintelligible, since the verb נוב is used only of plants; he proposes another verb ('nimmt er auch an Gut zu').
entries.flag: proposed verb garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Leg. ושתים, as Aquila and Symmachus (καὶ δεύτερον), joining אחת ושתים 'once and twice', i.e. repeatedly — cf. Neh 13:20 פעם ושתים, Job 33:14. זו שמעתי is relative to דבר אלהים: כי עז לאלהים, the power to punish the wicked, with v.13a the grace to reward the good.

entries.emendation: supply אָמַרְתִּי; divide the verse after אֲשַׁחֲרֶךָּ
entries.note: As it stands, an empty tautology; Ps 140:7 has the similar אמרתי לה' אלי אתה, so אמרתי has probably fallen out here. V.2 is in any case too long against the rest, so the part up to אשחרך must be severed as a verse of its own.
כמה is a hapax legomenon; leg. כלה (מ and ל interchanged, o. S. 134), parallel Ps 73:26 כלה שארי.

Symmachus ὡς ἐν γῇ and Pesch. איך ארעא = כארץ; the adjective must be congruent, ועיפה statt ועיף, as Ps 143:6 כארץ עיפה; and בלי מים is tautology — leg. אלי מים 'nach Wasser' (interchange of א and ב, S. 129).

'Schauen zu sehen' can only be excused by artificial exegesis. Statt חזיתך leg. אויתיך (interchanges of א/ח and ו/ז, o. S. 126, 132), giving the parallel of Isa 26:9 and an elegant sequence with v.2: כארץ ציה ועיפה אלי מים / כן בקדש אויתיך לראות עזך וכבודך — בקדש construes with לראות ('to behold Thy might in the sanctuary'), the psalmist being banished from it (cf. Pss 42-43, 61, 84).
'Besser als das Leben ist Deine Gnade' is impossible Hebrew phraseology. Leg. כרב חסדך, a frequent phrase, and לחיים 'for the living' statt מחיים (interchange of מ and ל, o. S. 134).
The incongruence is tolerable (3rd fem. plur. for masc. is frequent, cf. Ps 11:7), but possibly leg. שפתי שבחוך, the י dittographed. The verb שבח is Aramaic, found only in late pieces.
Despite the childish tautology of שפתי and פי the interpreters find nothing to object to. Leg. ושירי רננות (interchange of פ and י, and of ת and ר): 'in Jubelliedern wird mein Mund rühmen'.
'In the shadow of Thy wings I shout for joy' is senseless; leg. אתלונן 'I take lodging' — 'in Deiner Flügel Schatten weilen kann'.
Cannot be right, since דבק requires the preposition ב; leg. דלקה 'pursues after' (o. S. 130).
If b. is to cohere with a., תמכה must be imperative (penultimate stress) with ימינך as accusativus respectus, as Ps 60:7 הושיעה ימינך: 'stütze mich doch mit Deiner Rechten!'.

entries.emendation: לַשָּׁוְא; a verse introducing the foes is missing
entries.note: המה 'they'? — no enemies have yet been mentioned, so a verse speaking of them must have fallen out. And לשואה: LXX εἰς μάτην 'in vain', leg. לשוא.

First make the suffix congruent: יגירום (interchange of ה and ם, o. S. 132); the parallel is Ezek 35:5. The stem must be מגר, as Ps 89:45 מגרתה 'hingeben, preisgeben' — hence leg. a form of מגר here (and correspondingly in Ezekiel).

The foes themselves are surely not the jackals' portion — jackals are no man-eaters but haunt ruins. It can only refer to the foes' dwellings: בתיהם must have fallen out ('ihre Stätten werden der Theil für Schakale sein').
'How does the king suddenly get here?' A radical cure is needed: leg. ועבדך ישמח, as Ps 109:28 (interchanges of ע/ה, מ/כ, ד/ל, o. S. 126, 122, 127).

יתהלל requires the preposition ב (Ps 64:11 בו יתהללו כל ישרי לב); precisely because of the following בו the first בו must have fallen out. הנשבע בו means holding true to YHWH against the idol-cult (cf. Zeph 1:5); the close — the advocates of idolatry (דוברי שקר, cf. Isa 9:14, Hab 2:18, Isa 44:20) will be struck dumb.
More correct per LXX (ἐξελοῦ): 'mögest Du meine Seele retten' (the converse case 2 Sam 20:6, where Targum read והצר לנו for והציל).
מרגשת is not congruent with מסוד in a., which means secret plotting, while רגשה means loud raging. Vielleicht leg. a form of רגז, vexatio (the feminine occurs Ezek 12:18 ברגזה ובדאגה).
Unintelligible as it stands. Pesch. 'their words like arrows': leg. כחצים (the כ lost after the כו of דרכו), and strike the ר of מר — דרכו כחצים דברם 'wie Pfeile ihr herbes Wort abgedrückt'.
Pesch. ולא נתחזון, i.e. Niphal יראו 'they show themselves not' (not 'fear').
Grammatically inexplicable as it stands; leg. יתחזקו — they encourage one another with evil words to the evil deed (so Ibn Ezra, rightly).
יספרו 'erzählen'? Does not fit at all; he reads a verb of hiding ('sie verbergen sich, heimlich Fallstricke zu legen').
entries.flag: proposed verb garbled in OCR (יצפנו?) — verify at high res

entries.note: Statt למו Pesch. לן = לנו, or עלינו as Exod 5:21 ירא ה' עליכם: 'Wer wird uns sehen?'.
תמנו is explicable neither as 1st plur. nor 3rd sing. Targum ('to find pretexts to destroy the innocent') read תמימים or תם (as v.5), which fits excellently: they hunt for guilt in the guiltless.

entries.mt: חֵפֶשׂ מְחֻפָּשׂ וְקֶרֶב אִישׁ וְלֵב עָמֹק
entries.emendation: וְחֹפְשִׂים חָפֵשׂ מִקֶּרֶב איש ולב עמוק
entries.note: Wholly insoluble on the received text, but well explicable through Symmachus and Pesch. (Syro-Hexapla): the close read מקרב איש ולב עמוק, and the riddling חפש מחפש is participle with emphatic infinitive — the whole verse: יחפשו עולות תמים / וחפשים חפש מקרב איש ולב עמוק, 'they probe the inmost heart of the harmless to find guilt' (cf. Prov 20:27 חפש כל חדרי בטן).

entries.mt: וַיֹּרֵם אֱלֹהִים חֵץ פִּתְאוֹם הָיוּ מַכּוֹתָם
entries.note: Vv.8ff. become clear once the tempus historicum is turned to future, as the Greek versions partly and Pesch. and Targum consistently render (Aquila, Targum ויתקלון; even היו as future, Symmachus): 'Möge sie Gott mit dem Pfeile treffen'.

ויכשילוהו is correct (against the interpreters), the suffix referring to לשון; but עלימו is incorrect — leg. עמלימו (cf. Ps 55:16): 'ihre Schlechtigkeiten mögen ihre Zunge straucheln lassen', so that they accuse themselves. יתנדדו is from נדד 'weichen' (Ps 31:12), not from נוד ראש; ראה = plural participle ראי.
Symmachus and Syro-Hexapla 'they will see', which is more correct ('Dann werden es alle Menschen schauen'), with the following verbs likewise future.

entries.emendation: הַשְׂכֵּיל, the ו drawn to v.11 (וְיִשְׂמַח צדיק)
entries.note: השכילו is disturbing: unless one reads with Pesch., it is an infinitive pro finito ומעשהו השכיל, the final ו belonging to the next word — וישמח צדיק.
After ויתהללו supply בו from a. (cf. at Ps 63:12, o. S. 394).

That silence should be praise is a thought without analogy in Hebrew scripture — the Psalter constantly says the opposite, that God's praise be loudly proclaimed. LXX σοὶ πρέπει, Pesch. likewise: leg. נאוה as Ps 147:1; בציון metonymic for the Temple.
V.3 generalizes the fact that God hears the prayer of all beings; supply לכן before כל בשר יבאו.
The singular מני is incongruent with פשעינו; LXX plural (ὑπερεδυνάμωσαν ἡμᾶς): 'Hat das sündhafte Verhalten uns übermannt'. דברי עונת is periphrasis for עונות, like דבר רע.

LXX rightly render as perfect; vielleicht leg. לשכון statt ישכן. It refers in any case to the people privileged to dwell in the Temple courts — probably אשרי העם stood originally, as the plural נשבעה shows ('dass wir geniessen').
קדש היכלך is not intelligible (a superlative as in קדש משכני עליון will not do here); leg. as Ps 36:9 מדשן ביתך — here בדשן (ב and ק confused): 'der Fülle Deines Tempels'.

תעננו does not suit נוראות at all, even in the sense 'grant' (Hos 2:24); necessarily leg. תראנו (tempus historicum): 'Wunderbares zum Heile hast Du uns schauen lassen'. Per the parallel Ps 98:1-3 it alludes to the redemption from Babylon; בצדק is a Deutero-Isaianic catchword for the Heilsveranstaltung (cf. Monatschrift 1881).

ים is incorrect; Targum ('islands of the sea far from the mainland') = איי רחוקים 'die fernen Eilande', of which no prophet spoke as much as Deutero-Isaiah (66:19), the island-world (Asia Minor, Greece) having entered the oriental horizon through Cyrus' conquests.
'Girded with might' would be an insipid image beside מכין הרים בכחו; leg. נאדר בגבורה, as Exod 15:6 נאדרי בכח ('verherrlicht durch Allmacht').

entries.emendation: מוֹצָא וּמַעֲרָב(?), or מוּצָאִים 'those led out'
entries.note: Remains riddling: it cannot without more ado mean east and west. One could read מוצא ומערב (cf. Ps 75:7; Ezek 47:8), but מוצאי בקר is pleonastic and un-Hebrew; possibly it refers to those brought out (מוצאים) of the captivity. תרנין is in any case tempus historicum, causative as Ps 32:11.
The form is abstruse; simply leg. ותשקה 'and hast watered it'.

רבת is too much; the versions guessed right (LXX, Targum 'with produce'), but that does not lie in רבת. Its ת is dittographed as the ת of תעשרנה; the remaining רב transposed gives בר 'Getreide': 'mit Getreide hast Du es bereichert'.
פלג אלהים is the (rain-)cloud, a channel — parallel Job 38:25 מי פלג לשטף תעלה; leg. מפלג אלהים 'von Gottes Himmelskanal'.
Statt דגנם leg. דגנה, referred to the earth (interchange of ה and ם, o. S. 117, 132). But כי כן תכינה is inexplicable; vielleicht leg. כמסכן תכינה 'wie eine Vorrathskammer' full of grain.

The hardest verse of the psalm. נחת ('lay down'? 'wash down'?) with גדודיה 'clods'(?) is without analogy; LXX and Pesch. read 'fruits' (i.e. a form of ניב 'noble fruit') and instead of נחת a form of רבה. On that basis read 'Du hast vermehrt' with 'seine edle Frucht', and turn רוה into the perfect 'Du hast getränkt'; תמגגנה and תברך are tempus historicum.
entries.flag: precise proposed forms garbled in OCR (רוית? רבית ניבה?) — verify at high res

entries.note: עטרת is inexplicable in this context; leg. עשרת 'Du hast bereichert'. שנת טובתך is an enallage for שנה בטובתך.
Surely incorrect, for רעף is always joined with שמים and שחקים. Symmachus (Syro-Hexapla) 'from the richness of Thy clouds' — he can only have read a form of ערפל 'dichte Wolken'.
The Kal is simply transitive 'pour'; since it must here mean 'make fruitful', wohl leg. Hiphil.
'To gird oneself with jubilation' is an impossible trope; leg. a verb of singing, as Isa 55:12 ההרים והגבעות יפצחו רנה ('im Jauchzen jubeln die Hügel').
Not properly symmetrical, and כרים never means 'meadow' (o. S. 286); leg. הרים, in contrast to עמקים: 'die Berge sind mit Heerden bekleidet'.
Too tautological; Pesch. renders שימו by זמרו — leg. שירו כבוד (interchange of מ and ר, frequent).
Incongruent; leg. נוראים, the ם absorbed by the following מעשיך.
Incorrect, since the verb in the sense 'do homage, submit' occurs only in Niphal or Hithpael; leg. יכחשו (Niphal).

entries.emendation: supply אִמְרוּ before לכו וראו (per Pesch.)
entries.note: Pesch. has תאמרון before it — the verse (and v.6, save its close) is put in the mouth of the nations paying homage, who marvel at the Exodus and the Jordan crossing; עברו ברגל is perfectum historicum (so Pesch.).

entries.emendation: שָׂמֹחַ נשמחה בו, joined with משל בגבורתו עולם (v.7) as one verse
entries.note: The close belongs neither logically nor formally to v.6 (too long, unsymmetrical), and v.7 is also too long, its opening disturbing the parallelism — both may be joined into one verse. שם can be neither local (two localities are named) nor temporal (נשמחה is future): wohl leg. שמח נשמחה בו, the psalmist's summons 'wir wollen uns Seiner freuen'.
גוים would not be parallel to הסוררים; so here too leg. גאים 'the arrogant' (cf. S. 176, 179, 376).

Ketib ירים and Qere ירומו are both unfitting, and the proposed Niphal נירם after LXX and Pesch. is without analogy. Leg. 'those apostate from God shall be struck dumb' (ידמו, as Ps 140:9, where ידמו is even more necessary since the negation אל is lacking).
entries.flag: details of the redivision (אל → אֵל, attraction of מ) garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: השם gives no sense; leg. השמר 'Der unsere Seele am Leben erhalten'.
Leg. מצורה 'siege, Drangsal' (cf. Isa 29:3); so Symmachus πολιορκίᾳ.
מועקה is not Hebrew; leg. מוצקה. (במתנינו remains unintelligible; LXX and Aquila 'on our back'.)
Symmachus and Pesch. (לרוחתא) = לרוחה 'zur Freiheit, Erleichterung'.
